The paper was published in Materials Science Forum Vols. 730-732 (2013), pp 920-924
The research was conducted at the Departamento de Ciência e Tecnologia Aeroespacial, Instituto de Aeronáutica e Espaço in São José dos Campos, Brazil
Five different MWCNT concentrations were tested: 0.1%, 0.3%, 0.5%, 0.8%, and 1.0% w/w
Polyaniline was incorporated at a fixed concentration of 15% w/w in formulations that included it
The processed multilayer composites had a thickness of approximately 2.90 mm
The density of the processed composites was approximately 1.76 g/cm³
Individual impregnated glass fiber woven layers ranged from 0.45 mm to 0.65 mm in thickness
Maximum attenuation achieved was approximately 70% of incident electromagnetic radiation
The frequency range investigated was 8-12 GHz (X-band)
The NRL arch measurement technique was used for electromagnetic characterization
Glass fiber woven substrates were Plain Weave type with dimensions of 20 cm × 20 cm
Multiwall carbon nanotubes (Baytubes® C 150 P) from Bayer were used as the filler material
Nanocomposites with PANI/CNT showed only up to 20% attenuation, similar to pure glass fiber
The cure process used a heated press at 3 MPa pressure and 75°C temperature
Polyaniline was synthesized using dodecylbenzene sulphonic acid as the doping agent
A flat aluminum plate was used as the 100% reflector reference standard
The study measured attenuation properties on both sides (A and B) of the nanocomposite materials
Side A started with 0.1% CNT concentration while Side B started with 1.0% CNT concentration
The adhesion between woven layers was guaranteed by excess resin from the glass fiber prepregs
The materials were transparent to radar when PANI/CNT formulations were used (up to 20% attenuation)
SEM imaging showed that the impregnated formulations were well anchored to the glass fiber filaments
The study suggests that attenuation values may be higher for frequencies larger than 12 GHz
Electrical conduction in the composites was related to the amount of absorbing centers present
The multilayer structure with varying CNT concentrations provided superior electromagnetic performance compared to single-layer PANI/CNT formulations
